question: Do current public primary-source catalogues expose independently repeated scans of the same photographic plate that can separate material structure from scanner response?

primary_sources.title: A study of photometric errors on two different photographic plate scans

classification_rules.xy_segments: exactly two rows whose filenames end _x.fits and _y.fits
classification_rules.five_segments: exactly five rows whose filenames end _01.fits through _05.fits

applause_catalogue_audit.interpretation: Every apparent same-plate multi-scan group in the two relevant scanner families is a spatial mosaic, not an independent repeated acquisition.

heidelberg_sonneberg_pair_audit.hdap_query: SELECT plateID,object,dateObs,accref,accsize,pub_did FROM lsw.plates WHERE (object='Gamma Cyg' OR object='Gammy Cyg') AND 1=ivo_nocasematch(instId,'%Bruce%') AND dateObs>=36318 AND dateObs<36408 ORDER BY dateObs,plateID,accref
heidelberg_sonneberg_pair_audit.interpretation: The paper establishes the existence of paired scanner acquisitions, but the current public service exposes only the Heidelberg products and does not identify the exact 61-row subset or the corresponding Sonneberg files.

next_hypothesis: Require an independently mapped same-plate repeat or crossed scanner acquisition with exact product identities; do not reinterpret APPLAUSE mosaic segments or HDAP URL aliases as repeats.
claim_ceiling: Current public-source availability audit only; not scanner calibration, film-grain separation, material NPS, photographic-film stock response, or product evidence.
